question: When do children get interested in playing with building blocks?
solution:
The correct answer is '**12 - 24 months**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the details provided in the context of fine motor skill development, children start showing an interest in playing with building blocks between the ages of **12 to 24 months**.
 
• This stage of development marks when children are enhancing their hand-eye coordination and beginning to explore objects in their environment with more intention.
 
• Playing with building blocks requires some level of motor skill that children in this age group are developing, such as the ability to grasp, stack, and balance objects, which aligns with their developmental milestones around this time.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **0 - 6 months**: Infants at this stage are mostly focused on developing basic motor skills and sensory experiences. They are likely too young to show a specific interest in playing with building blocks.
 
• **6 - 12 months**: While babies in this age group start to grasp and manipulate objects, their ability to purposefully stack or build with blocks is still developing and not as refined as it is from 12-24 months.
 
• **2 - 4 years**: Children in this age range certainly enjoy playing with building blocks, but the specific interest and developmentally appropriate stage for starting to engage with building blocks as mentioned aligns with the 12 - 24 months period.
